text: 1863. Lincoln scribbles a speech on an envelope.
Nope. No envelope.
The Gettysburg Address: the envelope myth.
The story says he wrote it on the train.
Last minute, on scrap paper.
In fact, he started it in Washington.
The first page is on White House paper.
He kept revising it.
Five handwritten copies survive.
None of them on an envelope.
The speech was short. About two minutes.
The speaker before him talked for two hours.
Everett later said Lincoln got closer to the point in two minutes than he did in two hours.
So where did the envelope come from?
A popular story, written in 1906.
It said he wrote on brown paper, on the train.
Readers loved it. It became legend.
Lincoln was careful. Not a scribbler.
Envelopes involved: zero.
Anyway, here's Lincoln with his envelope.
